content_html:
This week Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg published a 6,500 word open letter titled "The Future is for Everyone".

But the BBC is more interested in why big tech executives keep writing manifestos about AI: [Zuckerberg's] vision echoes what AI leaders have expressed in various forms: the product they are building is among the "most important technologies in history." Marc Andreessen, co-founder of early web titan Netscape, perhaps started this trend in 2023 with a 5,000-word essay he called "The Techno-Optimist Manifesto", which argued innovation was the way to solve life's problems...

As the International Monetary Fund warns AI could affect nearly 40% of jobs and worsen global financial inequality, Zuckerberg says he believes there will be an abundance of jobs in the future. "I do not understand why anyone who believes that AI will eliminate most jobs and much of humanity's relevance would rush to build that future." Never mind that Zuckerberg's Meta has cut 10% of its global workforce — about 8,000 jobs — as the company reorganizes to focus on AI.

Zuckerberg's manifesto is the latest to land in our social media feeds in an effort to put a positive spin on AI. In 2024, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI boss Sam Altman released a manifesto called "The Intelligence Age", a sweeping expression of optimism about the tech's potential... That same year, in a manifesto titled "Machines of Loving Grace", Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei touted the potential of AI to transform everything from healthcare to politics.


So what's going on with these tech executives' manifestos? Economics blogger Noah Smith suggested to the BBC "they all feel like it's such an important moment that it's incumbent upon them to do whatever they can to shape the direction that this technology is going." Although he does see some value in their engagement with important issues. "Should we open-source something that has the ability to kill humanity? If you don't take that seriously, you're just a fool."

But Rob Lalka, a business professor at Tulane University, had a different explanation for the BBC: Lalka said the timing of Zuckerberg's manifesto coincides with rising anger over AI's impact on everything from jobs to the environment.

And while tech journalists and academics might pore over them trying to glean nuggets of meaning, these executive manifestos are not necessarily landing with the general public. "They're trying to make the case that the positives will far outweigh some of those negatives that the public backlash is pointing out," he said. "But I think a lot of the reasons for optimism are still yet to be seen."

content_html_zh:
本周，Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格发表了一封 6,500 字的公开信，题为“未来属于每个人”。

但 BBC 更感兴趣的是为什么大型科技高管不断撰写有关人工智能的宣言：[扎克伯格]的愿景与人工智能领导者以各种形式表达的内容相呼应：他们正在构建的产品属于“历史上最重要的技术”之一。 早期网络巨头 Netscape 的联合创始人马克·安德森 (Marc Andreessen) 或许在 2023 年发表了一篇 5000 字的文章，他称之为“技术乐观主义者宣言”，开创了这一趋势，该文章认为创新是解决生活问题的方法…… 正如国际货币基金组织警告人工智能可能影响近 40% 的就业机会并加剧全球金融不平等一样，扎克伯格表示他相信未来将会有大量的就业机会。 “我不明白为什么那些相信人工智能将消除大多数工作和人类的大部分相关性的人会急于建设这样的未来。” 尽管扎克伯格的 Meta 已经在全球裁员 10%（约 8,000 个工作岗位），因为该公司进行重组以专注于人工智能。 扎克伯格的宣言是最新出现在我们社交媒体上的宣言，旨在为人工智能带来积极的影响。 2024 年，ChatGPT 制造商 OpenAI 老板 Sam Altman 发布了一份名为“智能时代”的宣言，全面表达了对该技术潜力的乐观态度…… 同年，在一份题为“爱的机器”的宣言中，Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 大力宣传人工智能改变从医疗保健到政治等一切事物的潜力。 那么这些科技高管的宣言到底是怎么回事呢？ 经济学博主诺亚·史密斯向英国广播公司表示，“他们都觉得这是一个如此重要的时刻，他们有责任尽一切努力来塑造这项技术的发展方向。” 尽管他确实看到了他们参与重要问题的一些价值。 “我们应该开源一些有能力杀死人类的东西吗？ 如果你不认真对待这一点，你就是个傻瓜。”

但杜兰大学商学院教授罗布·拉尔卡 (Rob Lalka) 对 BBC 给出了不同的解释：拉尔卡表示，扎克伯格发表宣言的时机恰逢人们对人工智能对就业和环境等各方面影响的愤怒情绪日益高涨。 尽管科技记者和学者可能会仔细研究它们，试图收集其中的重要含义，但这些高管宣言并不一定会受到公众的欢迎。 他说：“他们试图证明，积极的一面将远远超过公众强烈反对的一些负面影响。” “但我认为许多乐观的理由仍有待观察。”
